Kubby Trial Now Delayed Again Until May; Prosecutors Actually Seeking Prison.

March 12, 2000

KUBBY LEGAL BRIEFING: 3/12/00

Last week, everything was on the line for us. If the judge ruled against us, we would be forced immediately into trial, without witnesses or the right to use the medical marijuana defense we helped put into law. If we were convicted on even one count, our attorneys told us we would be handcuffed, jailed and our children taken from us. It would takes months or years to win an appeal, long after I had died in prison from my cancer.

We faced a terrible choice: accept a plea bargain that would only require probation and save our family - or hold out for a favorable decision from the judge.

As the judge stepped onto the bench, one of the prosecutors turned and looked directly at me. He was smiling, thoroughly pleased with himself, and wanted me to know it. We were only about ten feet away so I could clearly see his face and his intent.

The prosecutor's smiling face struck me as incredibly rude, since Michele was next to me, crying her eyes out. I was trying to focus on the judge, but I couldn't stop wondering why the prosecutor was smiling and ignoring my wife's obvious distress. Then it struck me what was happening – the prosecutor saw her crying and assumed we were going to accept their plea bargain. Leering at us, the prosecutor wanted me to see how pleased he was
to have finally trapped his prey.

The judge told us we would have to make a decision on the plea bargain, BEFORE he gave his decision on whether or not to grant us a new trial and new attorneys. Then he asked me if we would accept the offer from the district attorney and all eyes turned to me. My answer cut through the prosecutor like a razorblade, " No your honor. "

Next came Michele. It would be all too easy for her to agree to one misdemeanor and walk away from this nightmare. Although she was still crying, her answer was brave and clear, " No your honor, I do not! "

Then the judge read his decision and to our everlasting relief, our continuance was granted. Our faith had been rewarded and the prosecutors received a major reality check.

Thanks to attorney Eric Berg's SEALED motion which disclosed several powerful defense secrets, including that our attorneys are prepared to testify regarding our INTENT to follow the law, our judge now understands our side. Judge Roeder even told the prosecutors, " Don't make a mountain out of a molehill, " and " Don't try to build your careers on this case. "

More good news Tony Serra has agreed to represent us in conjunction with Eric Berg. Furthermore, we are in the final stages of launching our national mailing, which we expect to provide a major chunk of funding for the battle ahead.

We are excited by the prospects of such brilliant defense attorneys (and their talented associates) working together. Michele and I believe this is just the beginning of a new alliance of attorneys and AMMA to actively defend the rights of medical marijuana patients who are being abused by the criminal justice system. We are committed to raising the money not only for our defense, but for the defense of others who are lawfully asserting their medical marijuana rights.

The police, prosecutors and elected officials of this state are massively violating our state constitution and our new medical rights. Together, we can help other patients under attack by law enforcement and prosecutors and force the authorities to obey the law and respect the newly granted rights of medical marijuana patients.

Let freedom grow,

-Steve
